cards.text: We're in the temple courts, and Jesus, God's Son, is teaching. This time, HE'S the one asking the question. It's about the scribes, the teachers of the law, and what they say about the Christ, God's promised King.

cards.question: Jesus brings up what the scribes teach. What do the scribes say the Christ is?

cards.text: Then Jesus brings up David, Israel's king, who spoke by the Holy Spirit and declared a line where the Lord speaks to someone David calls “my Lord.” TWO Lords in ONE line, and I'm on my third read with my mustache scratching my head.

cards.question: In David's line, what does the Lord tell David's Lord to do until His enemies are under His feet?

cards.text: Here's what Jesus points out: David himself calls the Christ “Lord.” A KING calling somebody else Lord is like me handing over my chef's hat, and friend, NOBODY gets the hat.

cards.question: If David himself calls the Christ “Lord,” what does Jesus ask?

answers.text: So how can He be David's son
So how can David be His king
So why don't the scribes call Him Lord

cards.question: There's a large crowd taking all this in. True or false: they listen to Jesus with delight.

cards.text: Jesus keeps teaching, and He says, “Watch out for the scribes.” Friend, when Jesus says watch out, I put DOWN the mixing spoon.
They like to walk around in long robes and receive greetings in the marketplaces. I've got a chef's hat taller than I am, and the only one on my planet who greets me is the oven timer.

cards.question: In the synagogues, the scribes want the chief seats. And at banquets, they want the places of ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus moves from what the scribes like to how they treat people. And friend, this is where I set my cookie down.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says the scribes defraud orphans of their houses.
Jesus says the scribes defraud widows of their houses, and they make lengthy prayers for a ___.
What does Jesus say these scribes will receive?

cards.text: Jesus sits down opposite the treasury and watches the crowd putting money in, and many rich people put in large amounts. The most money I've ever been near was my own 25-cent price sticker.

cards.question: Then one poor widow comes up to the treasury. What does she put in?

cards.text: All together, her coins are worth a small fraction of a denarius, like two chocolate chips left at the bottom of the bowl. Then Jesus calls His disciples over.

cards.question: Jesus tells His disciples, “Truly I tell you…” True or false: He says this poor widow has put in more than all the others.
How can the widow's two little coins be MORE than all those large amounts?

answers.text: She gave all she had to live on
She gave with a long loud prayer
She gave before anyone else did

cards.question: Jesus says the others all gave out of their ___, but she gave out of her ___.

findings.problem: The opening card identifies Jesus as the speaker and gives the setting and subject, but it never says whom He is teaching.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card adds facts not stated in Mark 12:35: Jesus is God's Son, the scribes are teachers of the law, and the Christ is God's promised King. Those outside-passage facts are given without their references.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Calling David Israel's king uses an outside-passage fact, but the card gives no reference for it; Mark 12:36 does not identify David as king.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.
